faqs.question: What is the Arc HPLC System used for?
faqs.answer: It's a versatile HPLC system for routine regulated analysis, built to receive transferred methods from other HPLC platforms and to modernize existing methods without redeveloping them.

faqs.question: Can existing methods transfer to Arc HPLC without changes?
faqs.answer: Waters states that transferred methods achieve equivalent test results while preserving analyte retention time and reproducibility, without compromising method integrity or changing validated gradient tables. Regulatory change control requirements remain the lab's own determination.

faqs.question: What is Gradient SmartStart?
faqs.answer: A tool that compensates for dwell volume differences between the sending and receiving systems during method transfer, adjusting at the system level rather than requiring the method to be rewritten.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 9,500 psi, across an operating flow rate range up to 5.000 mL/min.

faqs.question: How does Arc HPLC perform on USP assays?
faqs.answer: On the USP-NF assay for losartan potassium it met all system suitability requirements including injection precision below 0.5%, and led competitive HPLC systems on USP efficiency, USP tailing, and injection precision — with all comparison data generated concurrently in the same laboratory.

faqs.question: Does a quaternary pump compromise gradient performance?
faqs.answer: Waters' side-by-side testing on a challenging high-flow separation showed similar retention time stability and superior peak area repeatability compared with a competitive binary system.

faqs.question: Can Arc HPLC run smaller particle columns?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 9,500 psi limit allows high flow rates with smaller particle columns, so scaling from 5 µm to 3.5 µm gains resolution while reducing run time and mobile phase consumption.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions, on a stainless steel sample flow path.

faqs.question: How many samples can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Up to 768 positions using two 384-well plates, or 96 positions using 2 mL vial holders, in a 4–40 °C sample compartment.

faqs.question: How many columns can be installed?
faqs.answer: 1 to 3 columns, up to 7.8 mm internal diameter and 300 mm length.

faqs.question: Which detectors are available?
faqs.answer: Tunable UV, photodiode array, fluorescence, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, conductivity, electrochemical, and the ACQUITY QDa mass detector.

faqs.question: How is column usage tracked?
faqs.answer: eCord Technology tracks column usage and history automatically, supporting replacement decisions and batch investigations.

faqs.question: What software controls the Arc HPLC System?
faqs.answer: The Empower Chromatography Data System.

faqs.question: How is Arc HPLC different from Alliance HPLC and Alliance iS?
faqs.answer: Arc offers more pressure headroom than Alliance HPLC (9,500 versus 5,000 psi) for method scaling, and broader detection and multi-column capability than Alliance iS. Alliance iS leads on error prevention and guided operation.

faqs.question: How much bench space does the system need?
faqs.answer: 57.4 cm wide, 57.1 cm high, and 62.8 cm deep in the QSM-R, SM-FTN-R, 30 cm column heater configuration.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Arc HPLC System in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the pump, column, sample manager, and detector configuration required.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Arc HPLC System in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Waters Arc HPLC System in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

faqs.question: What is the Alliance iS HPLC System used for?
faqs.answer: It's an HPLC system built specifically for QC laboratories, aimed at first-time-right results, shortened release cycles, and fewer investigations through error prevention and guided operation.

faqs.question: How much does Alliance iS reduce human errors?
faqs.answer: Waters reports a reduction of up to 40%, based on their 2022 market research surveying 56 global pharma QC labs each running more than 25 systems.

faqs.question: What does the system check before a run starts?
faqs.answer: Pre-run verification confirms the correct column, the expected vials and plates, solvent levels, and solvent expiration dates before an unacceptable run can begin.

faqs.question: How does column tracking work?
faqs.answer: RFID-enabled eConnect Waters Columns are auto-recognized by the system, giving automated column history tracking for replacement decisions and batch investigations.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 12,000 psi, across an operating flow rate range of 0.001 to 10.000 mL/min.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.002% for caffeine under UV conditions, using flow-through needle injection on a stainless steel sample flow path.

faqs.question: How many columns and which detectors does Alliance iS support?
faqs.answer: One column up to 300 mm length and 8 mm internal diameter, with PDA and TUV detector options.

faqs.question: What sample formats can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Any three holders from: 48- and 54-position 2.00 mL vial holders, 96-well plates, 384-well plates, 48-position 0.65 mL micro-centrifuge tube plates, and 24-position 1.50 mL micro-centrifuge plates.

faqs.question: Does Alliance iS require Empower software?
faqs.answer: Yes. Informatics compatibility is Empower Chromatography Data System, Feature Release 4 with Windows 10 and later, and several features including pre-run verification and Method Matching depend on it.

faqs.question: Can existing methods be migrated onto Alliance iS?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Intelligent Method Translator App (iMTA) assists with migrating methods from other systems, and hardware compatibility with legacy methods preserves existing validated work.

faqs.question: What happens if an unsupported method is loaded?
faqs.answer: Method Matching warns the user at the point of attempting to run it, rather than letting the mismatch surface later during data review.

faqs.question: How does the system help when something goes wrong?
faqs.answer: Guided troubleshooting and guided maintenance run on the instrument touchscreen, with enhanced access to serviceable components and direct access to the Waters Help Center.

faqs.question: How is Alliance iS different from the Alliance HPLC System?
faqs.answer: Alliance iS adds 12,000 psi pressure, pre-run error verification, RFID column tracking, and guided workflows. Alliance HPLC retains a wider detection range, up to three columns, and broader software compatibility including MassLynx and third-party packages.

faqs.question: How much bench space and weight capacity does it need?
faqs.answer: 74.2 cm high, 49.9 cm wide, 63.5 cm deep, weighing 72.5 kg.

faqs.question: What is the Alliance HPLC System used for?
faqs.answer: It's an analytical HPLC system for methods development and routine analysis, built for standard HPLC workflows where consistency and compliance are the highest priorities — particularly regulated pharmaceutical QC.

faqs.question: How consistent is Alliance HPLC between systems and over time?
faqs.answer: Waters compared a carbamate separation run on two Alliance systems manufactured seven years apart and the results were equivalent, demonstrating both system-to-system and year-to-year consistency.

faqs.question: What is the maximum operating pressure?
faqs.answer: 5,000 psi, with a flow rate range up to 10 mL/min.

faqs.question: How many solvents can Alliance HPLC blend?
faqs.answer: Up to four, in any proportion, using Auto-Blend Technology, with 11 unique gradient profile curves for isocratic and gradient methods.

faqs.question: What is the sample carryover specification?
faqs.answer: ≤0.0025% for caffeine under specified conditions, and typically below 0.005% in routine operation, supported by active user-programmable needle wash.

faqs.question: What injection volumes are supported?
faqs.answer: 0.1 to 100 µL as standard, extending to 2 mL as an option.

faqs.question: How many samples can the system hold?
faqs.answer: Up to 120 vials, in an optional temperature-controlled environment running 4–40 °C, with STAT sample support and auto-addition.

faqs.question: Which detectors can be used with Alliance HPLC?
faqs.answer: Tunable UV, photodiode array, fluorescence, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, electrochemical, conductivity, and mass spectrometry.

faqs.question: Can mass detection be added to an existing Alliance workflow?
faqs.answer: Yes. The ACQUITY QDa Detector integrates into the existing workflow, and Empower 3 combines UV/Vis and MS data to give mass information for each peak in the separation.

faqs.question: Can Alliance HPLC run sub-3 µm columns?
faqs.answer: Yes. CORTECS 2.7 µm solid-core columns improve resolution and reduce run times when transferring methods from 5 µm chemistries.

faqs.question: Which mobile phase chemistries are supported?
faqs.answer: Reversed-phase, normal-phase, GPC, SEC, and IEX, all on the same system.

faqs.question: What software controls the Alliance HPLC System?
faqs.answer: Empower Software and MassLynx Software, with third-party software packages also supported.

faqs.question: Is Alliance HPLC suitable for GMP laboratories?

body.text: Alliance HPLC is a time-tested, dependable workhorse for HPLC separations, built for standard workflows where consistency and compliance are the highest priorities.
Waters demonstrated system-to-system and year-to-year consistency directly: a carbamate separation run on two Alliance systems manufactured seven years apart produced equivalent results.
Maximum operating pressure is 5,000 psi with a flow rate range up to 10 mL/min, covering standard analytical HPLC methods.
The quaternary pump blends up to four solvents in any proportion using Auto-Blend Technology, supporting both isocratic and gradient work with 11 unique gradient profile curves.
Solvent compatibility spans reversed-phase, normal-phase, GPC, SEC, and IEX chemistries on the same system.

Solvent delivery runs on a serial flow path with pulse-free delivery achieved without dampeners, alongside online vacuum degassing and automated solvent compressibility compensation for accurate flow.
A fixed delay volume in the integrated solvent delivery system keeps results consistent and predictable regardless of system back pressure.
Integrated seal wash is standard, supporting robust operation across all solvent types.
Sample capacity reaches 120 vials in an optional temperature-controlled environment running 4–40 °C, with active, user-programmable needle wash for low carryover.
Injection volumes run 0.1 to 100 µL as standard and up to 2 mL optionally, with STAT sample support and auto-addition.
Carryover is ≤0.0025% for caffeine under specified conditions, and typically below 0.005% in routine operation.
Column capacity is up to 3 columns as standard, with optional column heating, heating/cooling, or column switching.
Detection options cover tunable UV, photodiode array, fluorescence, charged aerosol, refractive index, evaporative light scattering, electrochemical, conductivity, and mass spectrometry.
CORTECS 2.7 µm solid-core columns can be used to gain resolution and cut run times when transferring methods from 5 µm chemistries.
Adding the ACQUITY QDa Detector brings mass confirmation into the existing workflow, with Empower 3 combining UV/Vis and MS peak data to assign mass information to each peak.
External control runs through Empower Software or MassLynx Software, with third-party software packages also supported.

That equivalence is what makes a method transferable across a fleet without revalidating each unit, and what keeps historical data comparable to current data during a trend review.
A newly manufactured Alliance and one several years into service behave as the same instrument, so age in the fleet isn't a variable that has to be tracked and compensated for.

High injection precision, repeatable and accurate flow rates, and exceptional retention time repeatability are the mechanisms underneath it — easy peak identification and precise quantification follow from them.
The fixed delay volume in the solvent delivery system holds gradient behaviour consistent regardless of system back pressure, so a column change or an aging frit doesn't shift the separation.

body: Baseline noise from pump pulsation is usually solved with dampeners, which add volume and slow gradient response. Alliance delivers pulse-free flow through a serial flow path instead, without needing them.

Online vacuum degassing removes dissolved gas before it reaches the pump, and automated solvent compressibility compensation corrects for how each solvent behaves under pressure, so the flow rate delivered is the flow rate set.
Auto-Blend Technology blends up to four solvents in any proportion, which means buffer composition and pH can be adjusted from the keypad rather than by preparing a new bottle for every condition.
Eleven unique gradient profile curves give real shape control during method development, beyond linear ramps.
Injection volume runs 0.1 to 100 µL as standard, extending to 2 mL optionally, so trace and preparative-scale injections sit on the same instrument.
Active, user-programmable needle wash is what holds carryover to ≤0.0025% for caffeine under specified conditions, and typically below 0.005% in routine work.
Integrated seal wash comes standard, protecting the pump seals across all solvent types — including the buffered mobile phases that shorten seal life fastest.
STAT sample support and auto-addition let a priority sample enter a running sequence without tearing down the batch.
